content.text:
We need to resolve March from Moat Cailin. Units present: two knights IDs 6 and 37. Reachable regions listed: greywater-watch (land, castleLevel 0), seagard (land, castleLevel 2), the-twins (land, castleLevel0), white-harbor (land, castleLevel1), winterfell (land, castleLevel2, controller Stark, triggersCombat true). Also can choose to stay. Need to consider supply: supply track is 3 (per house). Currently they have armies? Let's assess: Their armies: In Moat Cailin they have 2 knights together = an army of size 2 (counts as one army). In seagard they have none currently (they moved there earlier but then moved back? Actually after previous moves, currently seagard has no units (they moved from seagard to moat cailin earlier). So currently Greyjoy has an army at Moat Cailin (2 units). Also they have a ship at Ironman's Bay, a ship at Port of Pyke, plus footman? they have no footman. So they have ship units (fleet) maybe constitute an army: Ironman's Bay has 1 ship, Port of Pyke 1 ship. That's each single unit, not an army (size 1). No other armies.

Supply 3 allows army sizes: per supply table for 3: permitted army sizes 3,2,2,2 (four armies). So they could have up to 4 armies, with size max 3,2,2,2. Their current army at Moat Cailin size 2 fits. Moving both knights together to another area would keep size 2, still one army. Could split: move one knight to one destination, other stays (still army size1? Actually if single unit left, then that unit alone is not an army, no supply concern). The moved single unit also not army (size1). If both move to same destination, still army size2. So any move respects supply.

Goal: aim to increase castle control. Moat Cailin is a castle (stronghold? castleLevel 0? It's a castle area, controlled gives castle count). It contributes 1 castle area to our score. If we vacate without leaving power token, we lose that castle. With token we can keep. We have 8 power tokens, can spend one.

Potential gains: White Harbor (castleLevel1) currently neutral (no controller). Capturing would give us another castle (increase victory points). Also winterfell is a castle/stronghold (castleLevel2) controlled by Stark; combat needed.

Seagard is already controlled (controlledRegion list includes seagard, but they have control token there? board shows seagard has controlPowerToken: "greyjoy". Yes they control seagard already, no castle gain.

Greywater-watch is neutral (no controller). It is a land with no castle? castleLevel0, no castle. No gain.

The Twins is neutral, no castle.

Thus the best is to attack Winterfell for a stronghold (castleLevel2) which counts as one castle area (stronghold). That would give us extra castle area but involve combat, need to assess support.

Winterfell has garrison 2 (garrison token value 2). Units: 1 footman (id34), 1 ship (id34? Actually footman id34, ship id? there is a ship unit with id? The board shows at winterfell: unit footman (id34) type footman, and also there is a ship unit (the same id 34? Actually earlier units list shows at bay-of-ice a ship unit id34. At winterfell, there is a footman unit id34. Wait conflict: The board entry for winterfell: units [{"allegiance":"stark","id":33,"type":"footman","wounded":false}]. So only footman. The ship is at bay-of-ice (Stark ship). Garrison 2 adds combat strength for defender. So defender strength base: footman=1, garrison=2 =3. Potential support from adjacent areas: Need to check neighbours of winterfell. Let's call check_neighbours.

Neighbour list includes White Harbor (no units, castleLevel1). Also other neighbours: Bay of Ice (sea), Castle Black, Karhold, Moat Cailin (source), Port of Winterfell, The Shivering Sea, The Stony Shore. Support can only come from adjacent areas with Support orders.

Which of these have support orders? From revealedOrders list: Castle Black has Support +0 order (orderId 7). Karhold has Support +0 (orderId 8). Bay of Ice has Consolidate Power (not support). Port of Winterfell none. The Stony Shore none. White Harbor none. The Shivering Sea none.

Thus potential support for defender (Stark) can be from Castle Black (supports Stark) and Karhold (supports Stark). Support orders allow the owner to grant support to attacker or defender. Since these are Stark's support orders, they can choose to support either side? They could support themselves (defender) typically. They will likely support themselves.

So defender gets support from Castle Black (units: 2 knights) strength 2 each = 2*2=4. Karhold has 1 knight strength 2. Total support =6. So defender total combat strength = footman 1 + garrison 2 + support 6 = 9. Attacker (Greyjoy) would have knights (2) strength each 2 = 4. Plus March order bonus? This March order is March +0 (orderId 2) gives +0 combat modifier. No other mods. Potential support from Greyjoy to defender? Greyjoy might have support orders adjacent to Winterfell? Greyjoy's support orders: check list of their support tokens. They have only one support order placed at Greywater Watch (which is not adjacent to Winterfell). Greywater Watch is not adjacent to Winterfell (neighbors? Greywater Watch neighbors: bay-of-ice, flints-finger, ironmans-bay, moat-cailin, seagard). Not Winterfell.

Thus Greyjoy cannot support defender or attacker.

Thus combat would heavily favor Stark, likely lose.

Thus attacking Winterfell seems bad.

Alternative: move to White Harbor to capture castle without combat (no enemy units). White Harbor currently neutral, no units, castleLevel1 => capture gives +1 castle area. No combat needed. That seems good.

We also could move to Greywater Watch (no castle) or The Twins (no castle) maybe for future.

Consider supply and leaving power token: If we move both knights out of Moat Cailin, we vacate the castle (stronghold) and can place power token to keep control, preserving castle area. That costs 1 power token. We have 8 available.

Goal: we want to maximize castle count. Currently we have castles: pyke (stronghold?) yes castleLevel2 stronghold (counts 1), seagard (castleLevel2? Actually seagard has castleLevel2). That counts 1. Greywater Watch no castle. Moat Cailin is a castle (castleLevel1) counts 1. So currently 4 castle areas (as per strategic overview). If we keep Moat Cailin and also capture White Harbor, we increase to 5.

Alternatively, we could move only one knight out, leaving one behind to keep control without token? If we leave any unit, the area remains controlled automatically (no need token). The rule: If you vacate (all units leave) you may place power token to keep control. If any unit remains, you keep control without token. So we could move only one knight to White Harbor, leaving one knight in Moat Cailin, keeping castle without token, and additionally capture White Harbor (by moving the knight into neutral White Harbor). That would give us 5 castle areas, using no power token. However need to ensure after move, the unit at White Harbor will be the only unit there (size1, not an army). That's allowed. No combat. That's probably best.

Check if moving one knight is allowed: Moves list can have up to 2 groups, each group with unit IDs. We can send unit 6 to White Harbor, keep unit 37 in Moat Cailin, or vice versa. Must stay within supply: After moving one knight out, Moat Cailin will have one knight (single unit not an army). That's fine. Greyjoy will have remaining armies: at Moat Cailin (single), at White Harbor (single), maybe fleet elsewhere. Supply fine.

Thus we can set moves: one group destination White Harbor with unit_ids [6] (or 37). The other group could be omitted (unit stays). Moves list can have a single group (since other unit stays). That's allowed.

We must also decide leave_power_token: false because we are not vacating. So leave_power_token false.

Thus final JSON: moves list with one entry destination_region_id "white-harbor", unit_ids [6] (choose one). Could also pick both knights to move to White Harbor (size2 army) but that would vacate Moat Cailin entirely, requiring token. Better to leave one.

Let's ensure White Harbor currently has no order token? No order.

No enemy there.

Thus final answer.

moves.description: Destination groups and moving unit IDs. Unlisted units stay in the source. An empty list discards the order. Every group must be legal and fit Supply; an illegal final action is rejected without submitting the march.
moves.title: Moves

leave_power_token.description: Spend one available power token to preserve control when legally vacating the source area. This must be false if units remain or control cannot be established.
leave_power_token.title: Leave Power Token

actionOutputSchema.title: resolve_march_args
actionOutputSchema.description: You are resolving one of your March orders. Choose which units move and their destinations. Units you omit remain in the source area; you may split an army across destinations, and a single unit can march on its own. An empty moves list removes this March order without moving anyone. Only one destination may start combat. Use the reachable destinations in actionGuidance and keep the resulting armies within Supply. Leaving a control token costs one available power token and preserves control of the source when you legally vacate it. Compare castles gained and lost, and count support around the destination battlefield before choosing an attack. Before attacking another army, use check_neighbours on that battlefield to verify the supporting areas. Your final answer resolves this one order; another remaining order is a later decision.
